subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in doctor/config validate, hard validation errors, or startup/runtime warnings, and which catalog source is authoritative for custom and forward-compatible providers?
rationale: The source can identify configured refs, but warning versus hard-fail behavior affects existing custom providers, upgrade safety, and forward-compatible model names.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for unknown configured refs with wording that distinguishes trusted catalog absence from custom or forward-compatible refs.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs at config validation or write time, accepting compatibility risk unless an explicit escape contract is added.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup warnings, runtime errors, fallback notices, and status/doctor diagnostics instead.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for unknown configured refs with wording that distinguishes trusted catalog absence from custom or forward-compatible refs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest observed history across the model config, validation, and doctor boundary this decision affects.
